subject: c-info
title: C.INFO.------PROG.CONT.
description: Diagram in AF(D)-12 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One), second of two on book p84, paired with v2-p84-1. Continues the transfer-cycles argument: 'It then is important to view the many culture groups which have been on the planet as a means to understand the route of a given information thrust.' (C)C-INFO (the concept of composite information) is crossed with PROG-CONT (progressional continuance): the question is what composite-information produces when crossed with progressional-continuance — given that 'every cultural group has, on one level or another, utilized some (or every) aspect of principle information.' (R)TH-CONT (the reality of thrust continuance) sits between subject and partner. T-C-IMP (time continuum implications) drops from the stretch between the subject and (R)TH-CONT and carries (R)INT (the reality of intention). From the stretch toward the partner, SOC-RT (social reality) rises and CULT-INFO-DY (culture-information dynamics) drops; CULT-INFO-DY carries EXT-F (extended functionalism) and (C)MT-INFO (the concept of multi-information), which leads to BIA (bi-aitional). From BIA a bent line runs through AFD, at the bend, to (R)PART (the reality of participation). Structural argument: composite-information crossed with progressional-continuance is mediated through the reality-of-thrust-continuance. The multiple (c) and (r) prefixes distributed across the nodes registers Braxton's careful distinction between *concept-of* and *reality-of* — composite-information is taken conceptually (we are still analyzing the design), but thrust-continuance and participation are taken in their realized forms (these must actually obtain for transfer-cycles to read truly).
